metadata.title: Example Fellow — Claude, In Concert
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: if you install several plugins, do you have to tell Claude which one to use? Lands the carry-out that one plugin is a specialist, and a stack with intentional hand-offs is a coordinated team.
metadata.anchor_pair: B01 -> BCRY (must be the SAME stack composition)
metadata.one_flag: B25 — integration points still being built, a forward read not a settled fact
metadata.mirror_pair: B22 / B23 — stacked-holds vs. the habits that keep it holding
metadata.adaptation_note: Renamed teaching copy; source narration and beats retained. Not newly authored or rendered by Example Fellow.

beats.narration_text: Someone wondered: if you install several plugins, do you have to tell Claude which one to use? You don't — Claude reads the request and reaches for whatever fits. Here's how the stack actually works.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types the naive framing, hesitates on 'CHOOSE', corrects to 'tell Claude', lands the real question

props.text:
If I install several plugins,
do I have to CHOOSE
which one to use?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md. Writer types the newcomer's wrong-guess word 'CHOOSE' (implying manual routing), hesitates, corrects to 'tell Claude' -> lands the source reel's real question verbatim. Narration is 34 words + lead_silence_s 0.8, giving the typing a >=9s window (TIMING LAW; the 2026-08-27 pilot's 8-word narration produced a 2.86s open that never showed its own correction).

beats.narration_text: First, how the stack actually works.

production_viz.label: How a Stack Works
production_viz.mechanic: Act-header card: How a Stack Works

beats.narration_text: The natural guess is that you'd pick a plugin for each task by hand. You don't. With several active, Claude infers from context — the whole stack is available at once, and the request itself decides which layers wake up.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR PLANTED — the stack wakes on request

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR PLANTED — the stack wakes on request
production_viz.mechanic: The wrong guess ('pick one by hand') struck through; a request arrives, layered plugin cards (Marketing/Sales/Research/Data) fade in beneath it, dim/waiting. THIS EXACT STACK COMPOSITION RETURNS, fully lit, at BCRY.

beats.narration_text: Ask a marketing question, the marketing skills switch on. Ask a sales question next, the sales plugin engages. You change the subject — Claude changes tools. No announcement required.

production_viz.label: Topic changes, tool changes
production_viz.mechanic: One request branches live to the matching domain card as the topic changes; no announcement banner, no manual switch.

beats.narration_text: Ask something that spans both, and both contribute — Claude coordinates across the domains into one coherent answer, even though several specialized skill sets built it behind the scenes.

production_viz.label: Two domains, one answer
production_viz.mechanic: Marketing and Sales cards both feed lines into a single Answer card.

beats.narration_text: For a solo operator, that feels less like software and more like a bench of specialists on call — a whole team's coverage, answering in a single voice.

production_viz.label: A team's coverage, one operator
production_viz.mechanic: One operator card ringed by four output cards (Charts/Briefs/Contracts/Research).

beats.narration_text: And if you want a specific mix, you can just name it. Look at this from a marketing and a sales angle — and Claude applies both frameworks on purpose, instead of you hoping it guesses.

production_viz.label: Or just name them
production_viz.mechanic: Two named angle chips resolve in turn: Marketing angle + Sales angle.

beats.narration_text: The first hand-off: research into marketing.

production_viz.label: Research Into Marketing
production_viz.mechanic: Act-header card: Research Into Marketing

beats.narration_text: Say you're launching a new service and want positioning grounded in reality, not guesswork. First the research skills survey the landscape — who else is out there, how they position, and where the gaps sit.

production_viz.label: Survey the landscape
production_viz.mechanic: Competitor tiles flow in from the left toward a highlighted open-gap card.

beats.narration_text: Then those findings hand off to marketing, which builds positioning into the exact gaps the research just found — value propositions and differentiators aimed at open ground.

production_viz.label: Findings become position
production_viz.mechanic: Research-findings card feeds a gaps card, which feeds a positioning-built card.

beats.narration_text: The result is a stance that stands apart instead of blending in — distinct, not another me-too voice in a crowded market.

production_viz.label: Distinct, not me-too
production_viz.mechanic: A grid of identical grey marks with one distinct card standing apart.

beats.narration_text: Alone, research hands you intelligence and marketing hands you messaging — but messaging with nothing under it. Together the message is grounded. That's the difference between strategic and generic.

production_viz.label: Grounded, not generic
production_viz.mechanic: Two-bar comparison: a floating-message bar vs. a taller grounded-message bar.

beats.narration_text: The same hand-off, aimed at a meeting.

production_viz.label: Research Into Sales
production_viz.mechanic: Act-header card: Research Into Sales

beats.narration_text: You've got a meeting with a prospect, and you want to walk in better prepared than anyone they've talked to.

production_viz.label: Walk in prepared
production_viz.mechanic: A figure pauses at a doorway, prep folder in hand.

beats.narration_text: Research digs the background — what they build, who their customers are, recent signals. Sales turns it into a brief: your angle, the objections to expect, and what to lead with.

production_viz.label: Research + sales, one brief
production_viz.mechanic: Research card and Sales-brief card both feed into one Combined-brief card.

beats.narration_text: Under it, research produces the raw signals — recent news, hiring patterns, competitive position — and sales translates each signal into a move. Intelligence you actually know how to use.

production_viz.label: Signals into moves
production_viz.mechanic: Three signal cards branch to three matching brief-move cards.

beats.narration_text: A brief without research is surface prep. Research without sales framing is intelligence you can't act on. Together you understand both their world and your opening within it.

production_viz.label: Both sides, understood
production_viz.mechanic: Surface-prep and no-framing cards slide together and lock into one whole card.

beats.narration_text: Two more hand-offs that close a loop.

shot.new_visual_element: Two Hand-Offs That Close a Loop

production_viz.label: Two Hand-Offs That Close a Loop
production_viz.mechanic: Act-header card: Two Hand-Offs That Close a Loop

beats.narration_text: Data into marketing: feed six months of performance in — engagement, traffic, conversions by piece and by channel — and marketing builds next quarter's calendar around what actually moved the needle.

production_viz.label: Data builds the calendar
production_viz.mechanic: Performance-metric cards stream toward a next-quarter-calendar card.

beats.narration_text: Support into product: the support skills mine your tickets for the pain that hits the most people hardest; product turns the top three into buildable specs. You build against documented need.

production_viz.label: Tickets into specs
production_viz.mechanic: Many ticket cards funnel to a top-pain-points card, which fans out to three specs.

beats.narration_text: It's the shift from building what feels cool, or planning what you enjoy making, to working directly against what the evidence in front of you already says.

production_viz.label: Evidence, not intuition
production_viz.mechanic: A maker card beside a stack of real ticket cards, arrow pointing from tickets to maker.

beats.narration_text: Without the data, a solo operator plans on instinct. With it, creative energy points at the work that actually performs — the same effort, aimed better.

production_viz.label: Same effort, aimed better
production_viz.mechanic: A scatter of instinct-arrows resolves into one focused, accented vector on a target.

beats.narration_text: Both hand-offs share one shape: measurement feeds making. Data feeds the calendar, support feeds the roadmap — the loop between what customers do and what you build finally closes.

production_viz.label: The loop closes
production_viz.mechanic: Measure -> Make -> Measure-again cards, with a return arrow closing the loop.

beats.narration_text: The highest-stakes hand-off: a contract.

production_viz.label: The Highest Stakes: A Contract
production_viz.mechanic: Act-header card: The Highest Stakes: A Contract

beats.narration_text: A contract lands and you prep to negotiate. Two plugins stack on it at once: sales pulls up the whole relationship — prior conversations, the deal context; legal reviews the terms against its risk frameworks.

production_viz.label: Two layers, one deal
production_viz.mechanic: A contract card with two overlay layers stacking on it: relationship, then risk.

beats.narration_text: Legal flags the clauses that are unusual for a deal this size; sales frames the leverage you hold. The two merge into a single negotiation brief — what to push on, what's standard, and where you're strong.

production_viz.label: Two reads, one brief
production_viz.mechanic: Sales-relationship and Legal-risk cards merge into one negotiation-brief card.

beats.narration_text: You sit down understanding both the commercial relationship and the contractual fine print at the same time — negotiating from complete awareness instead of half of it.

production_viz.label: Complete awareness
production_viz.mechanic: Two parties at a table, a contract card between them.

beats.narration_text: Contract review in isolation misses the business context. Sales prep with no legal eye misses the risk. Stacked, neither blind spot survives.

production_viz.label: No blind spots left
production_viz.mechanic: Two blind-spot circles (business context, legal risk) overlap until the gap closes.

beats.narration_text: One rule holds the whole stack together.

production_viz.label: Keeping Combinations Sharp
production_viz.mechanic: Act-header card: Keeping Combinations Sharp

beats.narration_text: Four habits keep combinations sharp. Name the domains you want. Start simple — get fluent with one plugin before you orchestrate several. Document the combinations that work. And notice the gaps.

production_viz.label: Four habits
production_viz.mechanic: Four habit chips resolve in turn: Name the domains / Start simple / Document what works / Notice the gaps.

beats.narration_text: When a two-plugin flow keeps earning its keep — prospect research into outreach, say — write it down. Better, capture the whole workflow as a custom plugin, so it runs from a single command.

production_viz.label: A workflow, one command
production_viz.mechanic: Three repeated-flow cards (Prospect/Outreach/Send) collapse into one command card.

beats.act: ACT VI — 3 ONE FLAG + 5 direction B (where it flips)
beats.narration_text: One flag: this next part is a forward read, not a settled fact. When you wish a combination could do something it can't — data flowing straight into the roadmap — that's not a dead end. It's a signal: the integration points are still being built.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ONE FLAG — a signal, not a dead end

production_viz.label: THE ONE FLAG — a signal, not a dead end
production_viz.mechanic: A FLAG pill over a Data card and a Roadmap card with a named Gap card between them.

beats.narration_text: One plugin is a specialist. A stack, with every hand-off intentional, is a coordinated team.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the stack, fully lit

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the stack, fully lit
production_viz.mechanic: THE B01 STACK COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical geometry, every layer now lit, with the carry-out sentence beneath it.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. I'm about to make a real move — a launch, a pitch, or a build. Work it from two angles: research the landscape first and pull out the findings that matter, then hand those findings to marketing to build positioning into the gaps you found. At the end, show me exactly where the combined answer beats either angle working alone. Name the two domains, watch the hand-off happen, and you'll feel the stack do what no single plugin could.

props.command: I'm about to make a real move — a launch, a pitch, or a build. Work it from two angles: (1) research the landscape first and pull out the findings that matter, then (2) hand those findings to marketing to build positioning into the gaps you found. At the end, show me exactly where the combined answer beats either angle working alone.

beats.narration_text: Claude, In Concert.
…Liam, in for Bear.
